question: Should OpenClaw add a session-key pattern allowlist for `tools.sessions.visibility`, or fold this use case into the broader session authorization redesign tracked by related per-capability and A2A issues?
rationale: The requested config would define who may see, read, inspect, or message sessions, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent security model or operator UX.

options.title: Design one consolidated session policy
options.body: Treat #55420 as a tracked requirement and resolve it together with #48785, #57447, #53821, and #39102 so operators get one coherent authorization model.

options.title: Add a narrow allowlist mode
options.body: Implement `visibility="allowlist"` and `tools.sessions.allowlist` directly, with schema, docs, guard, migration, and security tests for every session tool.

options.title: Reject session-key patterns
options.body: Close this request if maintainers want per-capability or per-agent authorization only and do not want session-key pattern policy in core config.

recommendation.title: Design one consolidated session policy
recommendation.body: Treat #55420 as a tracked requirement and resolve it together with #48785, #57447, #53821, and #39102 so operators get one coherent authorization model.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent session visibility, config, docs, and hardening history makes them the strongest available owner for the security/product decision.
